rows.name: How to Control the Ether Jet
How to Start Nopon Grand Prix
Clear a new quest to obtain the Ether Jet!

A [System:Color name=arts_sp ]new character[/System:Color] has appeared
at Evac Ship Camp on the Giant God's Leg.

Talk to her and accept
the [System:Color name=arts_sp ]new quest[/System:Color].

Clear the quest and you will surely receive a [System:Color name=arts_sp ]wonderful
present[/System:Color].

※Drift: While turning above a certain speed,
release the accelerator to improve turning performance.
Watch out for forced dismounts caused by monster attacks!

Just as when traveling on foot,
monsters may [System:Color name=arts_sp ]target and attack[/System:Color] you
while you are riding the Ether Jet.

If a monster attacks you or inflicts
a debuff, you will be [System:Color name=arts_sp ]forcibly
dismounted from the Ether Jet[/System:Color].

You cannot ride the Ether Jet
while [System:Color name=arts_sp ]being targeted
by a monster[/System:Color], so be careful.
The Ether Jet can also be used in “Future Connected”!

After obtaining the Ether Jet in the main game,
it will also become [System:Color name=arts_sp ]usable in “Future Connected”[/System:Color].

As in the main game, press [ML:icon icon=btn_zl ]＋[ML:icon icon=btn_zr ] in the field
to mount or dismount.

release the accelerator to improve turning performance.
Take on the Nopon Grand Prix from the Main Menu!

[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Nopon Grand Prix[/System:Color] is now available.
(It may be unavailable at certain points
depending on story progress.)

Open the [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Main Menu[/System:Color] and press [ML:icon icon=btn_y ] to enter.
(You can also enter through the Nopon Assistant
near Raguel Bridge on the Giant God's Leg.)

There are [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Score Attack[/System:Color] and [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Battle Race[/System:Color] events.
Do well in each to receive
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]wonderful prizes[/System:Color].
Earn good results in the Nopon Grand Prix to obtain new equipment.

Fulfill the various [System:Color name=arts_sp ]reward requirements[/System:Color]
set for each course to obtain [System:Color name=arts_sp ]new
equipment exclusive to each character[/System:Color].

When your entire outfit uses [System:Color name=arts_sp ]the same series[/System:Color]
of [System:Color name=arts_sp ]new equipment[/System:Color], a special effect increases
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]acceleration speed[/System:Color] and [System:Color name=arts_sp ]boost speed[/System:Color].
[System:Color name=red_ex ]※This also applies in “Future Connected.”[/System:Color]

In Score Attack, earn as many [System:Color name=arts_sp ]points[/System:Color]
as possible [System:Color name=arts_sp ]within the time limit[/System:Color]
while making your way to the GOAL.

Touch the [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Ether Ore[/System:Color]
scattered around the course
to destroy it and add to your score.

You must pass through every [System:Color name=arts_sp ]checkpoint[/System:Color] marked [System:Color name=arts_sp ]NEXT[/System:Color]
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]in the correct order[/System:Color].
(The time limit is extended slightly when you pass one.)

Time Limit:
Score Attack ends when the count reaches
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]00:00.00[/System:Color].

Color Bonus:
Break three pieces of Ether Ore of the same colour
to trigger a Color Bonus and [System:Color name=arts_sp ]increase your score[/System:Color].
Aim for a high score with Color Bonus Chains!

Trigger Color Bonuses consecutively
to start a [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Color Bonus Chain[/System:Color]
and aim for an even higher score.

Fail to trigger a Color Bonus
even once and the [System:Color name=arts_sp ]chain
will reset[/System:Color], so be careful.
Learn to judge the size of Ether Ore!

There are two types of Ether Ore, [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Small[/System:Color] and [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Large[/System:Color],
and each behaves differently.

[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Small Ether Ore[/System:Color] awards only
a few points and does not
reappear once destroyed.

[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Large Ether Ore[/System:Color] awards [System:Color name=arts_sp ]more points[/System:Color] than
Small Ether Ore and [System:Color name=arts_sp ]reappears almost
immediately after being destroyed[/System:Color].
Raise your score even further with Large Ether Ore near the GOAL!

In Score Attack, Large Ether Ore appears
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]near the GOAL[/System:Color].

Reach the area near the GOAL as quickly
as possible, then [System:Color name=arts_sp ]keep destroying
Large Ether Ore until the time limit runs out[/System:Color].
This is the quickest route to a higher score.

In Battle Race, up to seven
characters compete to see who
can [System:Color name=arts_sp ]reach the GOAL fastest[/System:Color].

[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Ether Ore[/System:Color] is also placed throughout
Battle Race courses. Touch and destroy
it to earn [System:Color name=arts_sp ]points[/System:Color] and [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Color Bonuses[/System:Color].

You must pass through every [System:Color name=arts_sp ]checkpoint[/System:Color] marked [System:Color name=arts_sp ]NEXT[/System:Color]
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]in the correct order[/System:Color].

Elapsed Time:
The [System:Color name=arts_sp ]time elapsed[/System:Color] since the race started.

Position and Time Gap:
The number to the left of the icon is your [System:Color name=arts_sp ]position[/System:Color],
and the number to the right is your
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]time gap from the character in first place[/System:Color].
Destroy Ether Ore to keep your boost gauge filled!

Boost Gauge Recovery:
Destroying Large Ether Ore restores the boost gauge by
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]30%[/System:Color].

Boost Bonus:
Triggering a Color Bonus not only [System:Color name=arts_sp ]increases your score[/System:Color],
but also [System:Color name=arts_sp ]fully restores the boost gauge and makes it
unlimited for five seconds[/System:Color].
Gain an edge by choosing your route!

In Battle Race, the [System:Color name=arts_sp ]route
is up to you[/System:Color] until you
reach each checkpoint.

Jump off cliffs to aim for shortcuts,
search for routes that let you
destroy Ether Ore efficiently,
and find [System:Color name=arts_sp ]your own route[/System:Color].
Fulfill each course's reward requirements to earn rewards!

[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Every course[/System:Color] in Score Attack
and Battle Race has [System:Color name=arts_sp ]reward
requirements[/System:Color] and [System:Color name=arts_sp ]rewards[/System:Color].

The first time you fulfill a reward requirement,
you receive a [System:Color name=arts_sp ]first-time bonus reward[/System:Color].
From then on, you receive the [System:Color name=arts_sp ]base reward[/System:Color].
Choose a character whose stats suit you!

In Nopon Grand Prix,
the main game's characters can be selected
as [System:Color name=arts_sp ]playable characters[/System:Color].

Each playable character has different characteristics
and [System:Color name=arts_sp ]performance[/System:Color].

More playable characters become
available as you progress
through the [System:Color name=arts_sp ]main story[/System:Color].
Affects boost-gauge recovery speed and consumption.
Affects ease of turning and drifting.

Affects how much you slow down when hitting monsters
and your acceleration on slopes.

The following [System:Color name=arts_sp ]new courses[/System:Color] set
in Makna Forest have been added:
Score Attack: [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Jungle Rumble
[/System:Color]Battle Race: [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Midnight Forest[/System:Color]
New Courses Added: Imperial Capital Achamoth

The following [System:Color name=arts_sp ]new courses[/System:Color] set
in Imperial Capital Achamoth have been added:
Score Attack: [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Oval Achamoth[/System:Color]
Battle Race: [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Dawn Achamoth[/System:Color]

The following [System:Color name=arts_sp ]new courses[/System:Color] set on
Valak Mountain have been added:
Score Attack: [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Valak Slalom[/System:Color]
Battle Race: [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Blizzard Enduro[/System:Color]

The following [System:Color name=arts_sp ]new courses[/System:Color] set
in Colony 9 have been added:
Score Attack: [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Country Road
[/System:Color]Battle Race: [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Excite Colony 9[/System:Color]

Once you fulfill the reward requirements
for every course, the special effect
applies [System:Color name=arts_sp ]regardless of the armour you equip[/System:Color].
[System:Color name=red_ex ]※This also applies in “Future Connected.”[/System:Color]

This new adventure features [System:Color name=arts_sp ]major changes
from your previous adventure.[/System:Color]

The following pages explain the most important ones.

As you progress, you unlock [System:Color name=arts_sp ]a new special attack
to use in place of Chain Attacks.[/System:Color]

Reviving an incapacitated ally costs one gauge segment.

In this adventure, Shulk has already lost
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]the power of Future Sight.[/System:Color]

Be even more careful of monsters' powerful attacks.

・Allies who fight [System:Color name=arts_sp ]in a different style[/System:Color]
・Character Skills are disabled.

There are other changes too. Discover them as you play.

The Noponjaa are surveyors from Frontier Village, split into red,
blue and yellow teams. [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Recruit members of all three colours[/System:Color]
to let Shulk's party use [System:Color name=arts_sp ]new special attacks[/System:Color] with the Noponjaa.
Make sure to recruit them!

There are [System:Color name=arts_sp ]12[/System:Color] Noponjaa members in all.

Recruiting a member may reveal [System:Color name=arts_sp ]another member's whereabouts[/System:Color].
Known locations are marked on the map with [ML:icon icon=map01 ].

Noponjaa across the Giant God's Shoulder each seem to have
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]a problem[/System:Color] of their own.

Solve their problems and they'll join you on your adventure.

Under Collection in the main menu, the "[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Noponjaa Report[/System:Color]"
shows profiles of the Noponjaa you have recruited.

Noponjaa assist Shulk's party in battle as they please.

Each has a [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Speciality[/System:Color], such as restoring the party's HP
or inflicting debuffs on monsters.

Press [ML:icon icon=btn_b ] at the right time during Battle Start Bonding or
Burst Bonding and you may raise Noponjaa to [System:Color name=arts_sp ]High Tension[/System:Color].

Members with [System:Color name=arts_sp ]High Tension[/System:Color] fight hard without slacking off.

After a while, their Tension returns to normal.
Noponjaa Teams and Their Hidden Power

The Noponjaa have three teams: [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Red Team[/System:Color], [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Blue Team[/System:Color], [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Yellow Team[/System:Color].

If members of all three colours meet in one place,
rumour has it [System:Color name=arts_sp ]the Noponjaa's hidden power[/System:Color] will be unleashed...

Red Team has [System:Color name=arts_sp ]offensive[/System:Color] Specialities.
Blue Team has [System:Color name=arts_sp ]healing[/System:Color] Specialities, with some unusual members.
Yellow Team has [System:Color name=arts_sp ]debuff[/System:Color] Specialities.

Recruiting Noponjaa from all three teams unlocks [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Team Specials[/System:Color].

They cost three Party Gauge segments, damage monsters in a
wide area, and trigger a [System:Color name=arts_sp ]special additional effect[/System:Color].

Choose one of three additional effects when using a Team Special:
Red Meteoroid: [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Heavy damage[/System:Color] to one monster.
Blue Comfort: All allies gain [System:Color name=arts_sp ]HP recovery[/System:Color], [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Regenerate[/System:Color] [ML:icon icon=enh06 ], [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Debuff Immunity[/System:Color] [ML:icon icon=enh14 ].
Yellow Runaway: [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Force Daze[/System:Color] [ML:icon icon=enh39 ] and [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Strength Down[/System:Color] [ML:icon icon=enh27 ] in a wide area.

After recruiting a certain number of Noponjaa,
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Team Specials become more powerful.[/System:Color]

If all three allies can act freely when using a Team Special,
there's a small chance of an [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Extra Chance[/System:Color]. This lets you
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]use another Team Special[/System:Color] without spending the Party Gauge.
(You cannot choose the same additional effect as before.)

An Extra Chance is likelier [System:Color name=arts_sp ]the more Noponjaa are at High Tension[/System:Color].

After a Team Special, Shulk's party gains Tension,
but Noponjaa at High Tension return to normal.

Fogbeasts are stronger versions of ordinary monsters.
They also periodically emit [System:Color name=arts_sp ]riot surges[/System:Color] that draw in nearby monsters.

A riot surge forces affected monsters to attack Shulk's party.

They also gain the [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Riot[/System:Color] aura [ML:icon icon=enh35 ],
which [System:Color name=arts_sp ]raises their level based on the Fogbeast's strength.[/System:Color]

The [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Riot[/System:Color] aura [ML:icon icon=enh35 ] granted to monsters by Fogbeasts
can be removed like any other aura [ML:icon icon=enh35 ].

Remove the Riot aura's [ML:icon icon=enh35 ] level boost to get out of trouble.

Shulk's [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Monado Breaker[/System:Color] and Melia's [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Mind Blast[/System:Color] remove
monster auras [ML:icon icon=enh35 ], making them highly effective counters.
Inflicting [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Daze[/System:Color][ML:icon icon=enh39 ] on a monster also removes its aura [ML:icon icon=enh35 ].

If many monsters gain the Riot aura [ML:icon icon=enh35 ],
the Team Special [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Yellow Runaway[/System:Color] is especially effective.

It forces Daze [ML:icon icon=enh39 ] on monsters in a wide area, removing auras [ML:icon icon=enh35 ].
The Arts Manual Shop Is Open!

At the Arts Manual Shop, exchange [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Arts Coins[/System:Color] for
Advanced Arts Manuals of your choice.

[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Defeating Unique Monsters or Fogbeasts[/System:Color] may earn Arts Coins.
(You always obtain one the first time you defeat a monster.)

For Unique Monsters and Fogbeasts defeated before opening,
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]their Arts Coins are already yours.[/System:Color]

Check your coin total at the Arts Manual Shop.

Examine [ML:icon icon=map02 ] to watch a [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Companion Talk[/System:Color].

If you haven't met the conditions for viewing it,
come back once you've met them.

Once examined, a Companion Talk is added to "[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Companion Talks[/System:Color]"
under Collection in the main menu.

Use it to check the conditions for each Talk.

On the Giant God's Shoulder, the [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Ether Pick[/System:Color] lets you
mine [System:Color name=arts_sp ]gems directly instead of crystals[/System:Color] from ether deposits.

If you exhaust a deposit, come back after a while.

As the story progresses, you may obtain
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]a more powerful Ether Pick[/System:Color].

A better Ether Pick lets you mine higher-rank gems.

・Future Connected: Appearance now applies to Shulk's weapons.
・The main game's eighth Time Attack challenge is unlocked.
・The main game's Time Attack exchange adds [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Master-level Arts Manuals[/System:Color].
  Obtaining one raises the Art's level cap to XII.

[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Advanced Settings[/System:Color] lets you stockpile some earned EXP rather
than applying it to characters immediately.[System:Color name=arts_sp ]
[/System:Color]Open the System menu with [ML:icon icon=btn_plus ] and toggle [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Advanced Settings[/System:Color].
It is [System:Color name=arts_sp ]off by default[/System:Color].

Turn it on with [ML:icon icon=btn_r_stick_on ] to stockpile EXP from subsequent quest
completions and discoveries of Landmarks and Locations.

[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Casual Mode[/System:Color] lowers battle difficulty. Open the System menu
with [ML:icon icon=btn_plus ], then go to [System:Color name=arts_sp ]Options[/System:Color] > Game Settings to toggle Casual Mode.
If a recommendation to switch appears, press [ML:icon icon=btn_minus ]
to bring up the choice.

[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Event Theatre[/System:Color] has been added to the title screen.
You can rewatch events you have already seen.

You can change the following when watching events:

・Weather and time of day (some cannot be changed)
・Appearance equipment (already obtained)

Open the System menu with [ML:icon icon=btn_plus ] and adjust character levels in
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]Advanced Settings[/System:Color]. Levelling up consumes stockpiled EXP.
Levelling down returns the lost levels' EXP to your stockpile.
Any EXP exceeding the stockpile limit is discarded.

Levels are adjusted for each character individually.
Select the character and confirm with [ML:icon icon=btn_a ].

Choose a level with [ML:icon icon=btn_left ][ML:icon icon=btn_right ] and press [ML:icon icon=btn_a ] to adjust it.

When levelling up, the maximum available level based on your
stockpiled EXP is displayed. When levelling down, you cannot
go below the character's original level at the story's start.

Shops sell weapons and armour to help you on your adventure.

In this adventure, monsters do not drop armour as loot,
but you may obtain weapons different from those sold in shops.

People in this land also seem to have all sorts of troubles.

Completing quests earns money and rewards such as new equipment
colour variations suitable for Appearance.
Transferring Save Data from Nintendo Switch 2 Edition

If you return to the original version and play using
Nintendo Switch 2 Edition save data,
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]the added content will no longer be playable[/System:Color].

If you return to the original version,
the Ether Jet becomes [System:Color name=arts_sp ]unusable[/System:Color].

However, progress in related quests
and the Ether Jet you obtained are retained.
If you [System:Color name=arts_sp ]return to Nintendo Switch 2 Edition,
you can continue from where you left off[/System:Color].

If you return to the original version,
new equipment becomes [System:Color name=arts_sp ]unusable[/System:Color].
If it was equipped normally or for Appearance,
both will be [System:Color name=arts_sp ]unequipped[/System:Color].

However, you keep the items. If you
[System:Color name=arts_sp ]return to Nintendo Switch 2 Edition,
you can equip them again[/System:Color].

While riding the Ether Jet, picking up
collection items in the field [System:Color name=arts_sp ]restores
a small amount of the boost gauge[/System:Color].

Pick them up [System:Color name=arts_sp ]before the boost gauge is depleted[/System:Color]
to make exploration more comfortable.
